literal: A burden is great wealth for him who himself does not enjoy, to the worthy anything giving nature he who does not have.
translation: Vast wealth is merely a burden to the man who neither enjoys it himself nor has the nature of giving anything to the worthy.
modern: தான் அனுபவிக்காமலும், தகுதியுடையவர்களுக்கு ஒன்றையும் கொடுக்கும் குணம் இல்லாமலும் இருப்பவனுக்கு அவனது பெரும் செல்வம் ஒரு சுமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the futility of hoarding wealth without using it. The word etam means a burden, affliction, or disease, showing that unused wealth is not a blessing but a curse. The hoarder is described as someone who neither consumes the wealth himself nor possesses the natural inclination to give to deserving people. Thus, wealth without utility or charity becomes a heavy, useless load on its possessor.
